summary: Notion's internal integration is one of the quickest ways to call an API: create a connection in the developer portal, copy its token, and share the pages you want it to touch. For a multi-workspace product you create a public connection that uses OAuth 2.0. There is no mandatory review to use a connection; publishing publicly is optional. The one recurring gotcha is that pages must be explicitly shared with the connection before it can read them.

oauthAvailability.note: Public connections use OAuth 2.0; internal connections use a static token. Pages must be shared with the connection.
alternatives: Internal connection with a static API token for single-workspace automations
Personal access token for user-scoped scripts

approvalWait.note: No mandatory review to use a connection.

review.requiredWhen: No review is required to build or use a connection. Publishing a public connection broadly is optional.

prerequisites.detail: You must be a workspace owner to create an internal connection.

prerequisites.item: A connection created in the developer portal
prerequisites.detail: Choose internal (single workspace) or public (OAuth, multi-workspace).
Set under the OAuth configuration section; installation scope is fixed at creation.

steps.title: Create a connection in the developer portal
steps.detail: Create a new connection. For a single workspace choose an internal connection; for a product used by other Notion users choose a public connection that uses OAuth 2.0.

steps.title: Configure OAuth (public) or copy the token (internal)
steps.detail: For a public connection, add redirect URI(s) and choose the installation scope (any workspace or selected workspaces) under OAuth configuration. For an internal connection, retrieve the API token from the Configuration tab.
steps.gotcha: A public connection's installation scope cannot be changed after creation.

steps.title: Share pages with the connection
steps.detail: In Notion, open each target page, click the ••• menu, choose Add connections, and select your connection. The API cannot see pages that have not been shared with it.
steps.gotcha: API requests against unshared pages return an error; this is the most common first-run failure.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow (public connections)
steps.detail: Send users to the connection's authorization URL, then exchange the returned code for an access token tied to the installing workspace.

notes: Redirect URIs for public connections are set under the OAuth configuration section.
The installation scope (any workspace vs selected) is fixed at creation time.

recommended.purpose: Read pages and databases shared with the connection.
Create and update pages and database entries.
Append blocks and create new pages.

sensitive.consequence: Exposes user profile data including email; request only if needed.

notes: Notion's access model is capability-plus-sharing: a connection only sees pages explicitly shared with it.
Capabilities are configured on the connection rather than requested as granular OAuth scope strings.

blockers.title: API returns an error for a page that exists
blockers.symptom: Requests for a known page fail with a not-found or unauthorized error.
blockers.cause: The page was never shared with the connection via Add connections.
blockers.resolution: Open the page, use the ••• menu to add the connection, then retry.

blockers.title: Installation scope cannot be widened
blockers.symptom: A public connection cannot install into additional workspaces.
blockers.cause: The installation scope was set to selected workspaces and cannot be changed after creation.
blockers.resolution: Create a new public connection with the intended installation scope.
